subject: WRITE statement
notes: RULE (cite.py --check 14.9.51.3 'The BEFORE and AFTER phrases shall not both be specified if the PAGE phrase is specified' -> OK 14.9.51.3 17). BOTH DIRECTIONS OBSERVED. The prohibition: tests/conformance/negative/pb712-write-before-after-page.cob writes `WRITE P-REC BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING PAGE` and is refused COBOL1910 at 2023. The complement (the pair WITHOUT the PAGE operand is legal, so the rule is a narrowing and not a ban): tests/conformance/2023/write_before_and_after.cob compiles and runs `BEFORE AFTER ADVANCING 3 LINES` and `AFTER BEFORE ADVANCING 2 LINES`. WHY SR17 EXISTS, which is what makes the check's placement correct rather than arbitrary: 14.9.51.4 GR25 g) and h) position the record 'before or after (depending on the phrase used) the device is repositioned' to the next page, and with both words written there is no phrase to depend on -- whereas GR25 e)/f), which govern the numeric and mnemonic operands, DO resolve the pair (f)'s second sentence puts its advance after the presentation). EDITIONS 2023: the pair itself is a COBOL-2023 introduction (Annex E.3.3 item 2; docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 45), so below 2023 this source is refused first by the introduction gate COBOL0900, evidenced by conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb712-write-before-after-below-2023 and conformance:cases/_unassigned/pb712-write-after-before-below-2023. kb/Work PB712 (LANDED 2026-09-06) is the note; before it the SR17 test was one arm of a malformed-pair check over a two-ADVANCING-phrase grammar 14.9.51.2 Format 1 never prints.
